candidates.attacker_control: Unauthenticated attacker supplies j_username (configured escape-hatch username, typically a well-known alias such as admin) and an empty j_password to the authentication gateway POST /securityRealm/escapeHatch (getAuthenticationGatewayUrl(), 866-869), reaching the AuthenticationManager in createSecurityComponents() and checkEscapeHatch(). EscapeHatchCrumbExclusion also exempts that path from CSRF crumb validation.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified there is no doCheckEscapeHatch* validation (all checkPermission sites enumerated) and no non-empty assertion in constructor/readResolve; escape hatch is off by default and rejected in FIPS mode; Util.fixEmptyAndTrim is applied to username/group but not to the Secret; if the blank field binds to null instead of Secret.fromString(""), the check throws rather than authenticating.
candidates.impact: Authentication bypass of the break-glass account: any network user knowing/guessing the escape-hatch username obtains an authenticated Jenkins session; with a configured administrative escapeHatchGroup (the typical purpose of the feature) this is effectively full Jenkins compromise. The same missing validation also makes an enabled-but-unset secret throw IllegalArgumentException inside checkEscapeHatch, breaking the recovery path.
candidates.prerequisites: Escape hatch enabled (non-default) with a non-empty escapeHatchUsername and a secret stored as an empty value (blank Secret field / empty JCasC value). If the secret is left null, BCrypt.checkpw(password, null) throws instead (counter-case). If escapeHatchGroup is configured, the authenticated principal also receives that group's authorities.
candidates.root_cause: OicSecurityRealm.setEscapeHatchSecret(Secret) (lines 791-803) hashes whatever string it receives: if the value is not already a BCrypt hash it stores Secret.fromString(BCrypt.hashpw(escapeHatchString, BCrypt.gensalt())). An empty secret thus becomes a valid BCrypt hash of the empty string. checkEscapeHatch() (805-809) only tests username.equals(escapeHatchUsername) and BCrypt.checkpw(password, Secret.toString(escapeHatchSecret)) — there is no check that password/hash are non-empty. Nothing else enforces it: setEscapeHatchEnabled() (778-783) only performs a FIPS check, the constructor/readResolve do not validate the pair, and DescriptorImpl (1527-1631) exposes no doCheckEscapeHatchSecret/Username validation, so the config UI saves escapeHatchEnabled=true with a blank secret field.
candidates.title: Escape hatch accepts an empty password when configured with an empty secret (missing non-empty validation of the recovery secret)
candidates.trace: 1) Admin enables the escape hatch, sets username/group, leaves the secret blank; BCryptPattern does not match '' so setEscapeHatchSecret hashes the empty string (791-803). 2) Attacker POSTs j_username=<escapeHatchUsername>&j_password= to /securityRealm/escapeHatch. 3) authenticate() (893-921) runs randomWait() then checkEscapeHatch(): username match is true and BCrypt.checkpw("", hash-of-"") returns true (805-809). 4) A UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken(escapeHatchUsername, "", [AUTHENTICATED, escapeHatchGroup]) is set in the SecurityContext and SecurityListener.fireAuthenticated2() fires (904-914), creating a session as the escape-hatch user. 5) handleTokenExpiration() then returns true for that principal because it has no OicCredentials property (1379-1383), so no OIDC expiry enforcement applies.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. Could not verify in-snapshot how Stapler/JSON binding represents a blank Secret field (empty vs null) nor how Jenkins core's authentication filter forwards an empty j_password; Jenkins core and pac4j sources are absent from the tree.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-521 / improper authentication: privileged recovery credential not validated as non-empty (empty password accepted)

coverage_summary: All 108 assigned files were enumerated; all 17 src/main Java classes were read (OicSecurityRealm.java end-to-end in overlapping ranges), plus resource bundles/help files, the JS toggle, Markdown docs and Maven/GitHub workflow config. Reviewed surfaces: commence/finish login flow and redirect validation, escape-hatch authentication, CSRF crumb exclusions, API-token/expiry handling and refresh flow, logout/end-session URL construction, FIPS-140 algorithm filtering, TLS-verification bypass options, resource-retriever settings, JMESPath claim extraction, and all DescriptorImpl form-validation methods (all ADMINISTER-gated, @POST/@RequirePOST). No test sources or Jelly views exist in the snapshot, and Jenkins core/pac4j are not included, so those layers were reasoned about from call sites only.
limitations: Source-level review only; no execution, dependency resolution, or runtime confirmation.

Jenkins core 2.479.x and pac4j 6.1.0 sources are absent, so Stapler annotation inheritance, blank-Secret form binding, core API-token Basic-auth fallback, UserProperty.reconfigure reachability, and OIDC state/nonce defaults could not be verified.
No tests or Jelly views are present, so UI wiring and regression coverage could not be inspected.

Per the one-candidate cap, rejected leads (well-known cache inversion, crumb-exclusion CSRF, unguarded Basic parsing, user-rebindable OicCredentials, logout @RequirePOST) were not investigated to exhaustion.
The selected candidate depends on a reachable but unusual configuration (escape hatch enabled with an empty secret) and on a blank Secret field binding to an empty Secret rather than null.

rejected_leads.lead: EscapeHatchCrumbExclusion unconditionally exempts POST /securityRealm/escapeHatch from CSRF crumb validation, with no realm/enabled check (unlike OicCrumbExclusion).
rejected_leads.reason: Documented as intentional for the login gateway; the sibling realm check adds nothing when it matters. Worst case is low-impact login CSRF, not a distinct vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: OicServerWellKnownConfiguration.toProviderMetadata() (88-92) inverts its freshness test (returns cache when wellKnownExpires.isBefore(now), comment says 'still fresh'; re-downloads while fresh; setWellKnownExpires(null) always sets now+1h at 143/165-180).
rejected_leads.reason: Clear logic bug but weak/unproven security impact: stale issuer/JWKS/token endpoints retained after idle and extra outbound fetch per commenceLogin while fresh, with no attacker-controlled path to substitute metadata.

rejected_leads.lead: handleTokenExpiration() (1360-1373) uses split(":")[1] and ApiTokenProperty.matchesPassword without null/length guards when allowTokenAccessWithoutOicSession is enabled.
rejected_leads.reason: Malformed Authorization can throw AIOOBE/NPE and yield HTTP 500, but it is request-scoped robustness reachable only by an authenticated user with the option enabled.

rejected_leads.lead: getValidRedirectUrl() (931-950) prefix check redirectUrl.startsWith(rootUrl) as a possible open redirect.
rejected_leads.reason: Jenkins root URLs end with '/', which the plugin itself relies on (buildOAuthRedirectUrl concatenates without separator), so host-suffix confusion fails the check; the historic open-redirect fix is present.

rejected_leads.lead: OicCredentials.reconfigure() (25-29) binds user-config JSON onto a property holding tokens and expiresAtMillis.
rejected_leads.reason: Would let a user extend their own session, but the class has no setters and final private fields so JSON binding appears ineffective; reachability could not be verified. Unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: doLogout() override (1169-1190) lacks @RequirePOST (possible logout CSRF via GET).
rejected_leads.reason: Stapler annotation inheritance and dispatch target (/logout vs /securityRealm/logout) could not be established from the snapshot; impact would be forced logout only.

rejected_leads.lead: AnythingGoesTokenValidator / disableTokenVerification (527-534) accepts any parseable ID token (no signature/nonce).
rejected_leads.reason: Explicit, documented admin opt-in blocked in FIPS mode; insecure configuration rather than an unauthenticated bypass (code exchange with client secret still required).

summary: Reviewed the oic-auth plugin snapshot (108 files; all 17 src/main Java classes read, plus resources, docs, build files). No tests or Jelly views are present and Jenkins core/pac4j sources are not in the tree, so framework behaviour could only be reasoned about. Strongest source-evidenced weakness: escape-hatch credential handling — any non-null secret (including an empty string) is BCrypt-hashed and checked with BCrypt.checkpw without ever requiring the recovery secret/password to be non-empty, so an escape hatch enabled with a blank secret authenticates an empty password from an unauthenticated POST to /securityRealm/escapeHatch. Other suspicious areas are listed as rejected/unconfirmed leads.
